messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a manual `terraform import` for module.k8s_secret.xf_secret in staging and now `terraform apply` is hanging with a replace on the k8s secret. not sure if i messed up the import mapping. anyone around to quick-check?

Tina: :eyes: pinging infra oncall — can you paste the import command you used?

alex: sure — ran:
```
terraform import module.k8s_secret.kv[0] kubernetes_secret.xf-service-secret
```
then `terraform plan` shows: `~ resource "kubernetes_secret" "xf-service-secret" (tainted)` and then later a replacement.

jon: are you seeing a state entry for the secret after the import? `terraform state list | grep xf-service-secret`

alex: yep it shows up: `module.k8s_secret.kv[0]` in state. apply stalls after creating some dependent configmap, then waits on kube API and times out.

maria: could be a label/annotation drift causing k8s provider to think recreate is necessary. did you import the exact set of attributes? imports only map ID, not all attrs. check `kubectl get secret xf-service-secret -n staging -o yaml` vs tf config for annotations/immutable flag.

alex: good point — the cluster secret has `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` present and our tf doesn't include that. but should that cause a replace?

jon: usually not. more likely something like `type` or `immutable` changed. also if the provider sees a mismatch in `data`/`stringData` it may attempt to replace depending on lifecycle rules.

alex: running this to get diffs:
```bash
kubectl get secret xf-service-secret -n staging -o yaml > /tmp/secret.yaml
terraform show -json tfplan.out | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.address=="module.k8s_secret.kv[0]")'
```

Tina: ops-bot from earlier runs, was there a taint left on that resource? ops-bot: any recent automated taints?

ops-bot: recent: no automated taints on module.k8s_secret.kv[0] in the last 24h. last taint by user: deploy-bot at 3349950000 for emergency rotate.

maria: if the import didn’t capture provider-specific ID (like namespace/name) exactly, you'll get drift. try `terraform state show module.k8s_secret.kv[0]` and compare `metadata[0].annotations` and `type`. If only annotations differ, consider adding `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata] }` temporarily to avoid replace while you reconcile.

alex: doing state show now. also should i try `terraform import -allow-missing-config`? i didn't use that flag.

jon: that flag can help if the resource is managed outside of tf, but it won't populate attributes. If you want a safe path, add `lifecycle.ignore_changes` for metadata, run `terraform plan` to verify no destroy/create, then remove the ignore after aligning TF config to cluster state and run `plan` again.

alex: ok i'll add lifecycle ignore for annotations and re-run plan. will report back in ~10m. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

(10m later)

alex: update — added `ignore_changes = [metadata]`, plan now shows no replace. i removed the taint and applied successfully. i pushed a follow-up PR to update TF to match the cluster annotations so we can remove the ignore next deploy.

Tina: nice. can you drop the PR link here so we can review? also add a note in the apply run that you used ignore_changes temporarily.

alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/5123 — description explains the mismatch and steps to reconcile.

maria: perfect. one more thing — please run `terraform state rm module.k8s_secret.kv[0]` only if you intend to completely adopt out-of-band management. otherwise keep state synced.

alex: yep not removing state. marking resolved. thanks team.
